messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy v2.3.4 -> service-inference reported error rate jump to 8.9% (baseline 0.4%) at 1775247890. Canary weight=10%. Logs attached.

alyssa: paging @oncall-sre — seeing user-facing 5xxs for a subset of requests after the canary flip. Notably lower qps, but higher failure rate.

oncall-sre: I’m on it. joining voice. Can someone drop the canary URL and example request/response pair?

michael: sample request: POST /v1/generate payload, got 502 with traceback: `RuntimeError: kv-cache OOM during warmup` — only seen on models with long context. Appears after ~30s of steady traffic. Logs:```
[service-infer][error] kv_cache_alloc failed at shard 3
[worker-12] oom while warmup, aborting request
```

alyssa: ops-runner just flipped the feature flag `ff/new-attn-path` to on for 10% canary at 16:44 UTC. No DB migrations.

ops-runner: confirmed. flag flip command: `redwood feature set ff/new-attn-path on --percent=10 --env=prod`

oncall-sre: ok quick assessment: consistent with a kernel path that increases memory per-inflight kv cache. Two mitigation options: 1) kill the flag (immediate low-risk revert) or 2) revert canary deployment (slightly slower, full deploy rollback). Recommend kill the flag first to reduce blast. Who can flip?

ops-runner: I can flip now. Will do a controlled kill-switch and monitor metrics.

product-ops: heads-up — a handful of large-customer sessions hit errors (we track via cust-tag). CSbot will chime in if support tickets escalate.

ops-runner: flipping flag to off for 100% of canary cohort... `redwood feature set ff/new-attn-path off --cohort=canary` -> response OK.

deploy-bot: Feature flag change: ff/new-attn-path set to OFF by ops-runner at 1775248004. Canary traffic should route to previous path within the next 10s.

oncall-sre: monitoring... error rate dropping back toward baseline. Token-level errors falling. Still seeing a few spillover 502s; tail latency elevated. Running `ps` and memcheck on workers.

michael: mem profiles show per-request mem spike ~1.8GB vs baseline 0.6GB for affected model version. Likely leak in the new attention kernel under long seqs.

alyssa: thanks. action items: (1) keep flag OFF for canary, (2) hold full rollout until kernel fix, (3) open a patch ticket for runtime team, (4) inform CS and document incident. Anyone want to take on immediate customer comms?

customer-success-bot: Notifying CS on-call. Will prepare a short templated message for customers impacted: "We observed elevated inference errors affecting a subset of long-context requests after a canary evaluation. We reverted the canary feature flag and services are recovering. Investigating root cause and will follow up."

eva: I’ll take the root cause and follow-up write-up once we have repro and a fix. Assigning to eng-runtime (ticket #ENG-5492).

oncall-sre: quick verification checklist run:
- confirm flag is off -> `redwood feature get ff/new-attn-path` shows OFF (done)
- alerting suppressed for downstream flapping (tuned)
- canary weight 0% (confirmed)
- observe steady-state for 15m before closing incident

ops-runner: metrics at +5m: error rate back to 0.45%, p99 latency improving. will keep 15m watch and then handoff to evan on-call for postmortem.

alyssa: Handoff plan: oncall-sre -> eva for RCA and remediation tracking. Assigning followup meeting 1hr to sync with runtime and QA. I'll update the incident channel with timeline + customers impacted.

oncall-sre: One more note — if we see reappearance after kernel hotfix, prefer a canary rollback to previous compiled kernel rather than feature flag flip, since the flag masks behavior in runtime path. Record that for playbook.

michael: created temporary QA harness to reproduce with long-context payloads. Will paste repro steps in ENG ticket.

ops-runner: closing the active page. Will reopen if metrics deviate.

deploy-bot: Incident ack by oncall-sre at 1775248235. Status: mitigated (flag revert).

alyssa: thanks everyone — doc ops: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1775247890 (I'll populate timeline). Follow-up owners: eva (RCA), michael (repro/fix PR), ops-runner (deploy guard adjustments).
